approved_scope.title: Rs-lint: Rust qualification fails on unformatted or clippy-warning Rust code: qualify.py rs runs cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings in rs/ before the tests, so hosted CI catches what the rs verify lane catches
approved_scope.description: rs-lint: Rust qualification fails on unformatted or clippy-warning Rust code: qualify.py rs runs cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings in rs/ before the tests, so hosted CI catches what the rs verify lane catches
acceptance_criteria: qualify.py rs runs cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings in rs/ after the lockfile is generated and before cargo test, records the rustfmt and clippy versions, and exits non-zero on a formatting diff or any clippy warning (a release test asserts both commands are in the rs lane, and a local probe with one unformatted line and one clippy warning each makes qualify.py rs fail); hosted Rust CI and the publish-crates qualification step therefore enforce formatting and lints with no workflow change; the current tree passes both.

answers.constraints: REQ-release-2: qualification stays read-only with no publish credentials, so only qualify.py changes and no workflow gains a permission or step. The rustup stable toolchain on ubuntu-latest is unpinned, so a new stable clippy lint can fail qualification (and the publish-crates qualification step) without a code change; that is accepted and would be fixed in a follow-up, not by weakening -D warnings.
